subject: SLA waiver request — content safeguard caused structured-output failures
messages:
From: ops+platform@novihealth.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T16:25:00Z
Subject: Production outage: structured output failing when content guard triggers

Markus / Redwood team,

We observed a regression this morning where several of our downstream services started receiving malformed JSON from the structured-output endpoint. The issue coincided with a content-safeguard hit — the model returned a safeguard result that caused our parser to throw. This impacted billing and two transaction flows for about ~47 minutes (11:12–11:59 PT).

Highlights: 
- Endpoint: POST /v1/chat/structured-output (region us-west-2)
- Model: rwinf-open-7b-v2 (pinned)
- Error mode: safeguard block returned plain-text instead of JSON-schema wrapper
- Customer impact: failed transaction enrichment (payment metadata) and a delayed notification queue

We attached exported payloads and a short csv showing request ids. We need: 1) an expedited incident assessment (what caused the guard to return a non-structured response), 2) an immediate mitigation path (preferably a short-lived routing rule that bypasses the strictest guard for our transaction queue), and 3) an SLA credit/waiver request given this produced user-visible downtime.

This is high priority for NoviHealth (HIPAA-adjacent workloads). Please loop in whoever owns runtime/carveouts and security.

Thanks,
Sara Lee
Senior Platform Engineer — NoviHealth
ops+platform@novihealth.com

Attachments: novi_incident_payloads.csv, novi_filtered_sample.txt

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: ops+platform@novihealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Production outage: structured output failing when content guard triggers

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I'm very sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as an incident with the highest priority.

Immediate asks from our side: 
- Can you confirm the request-ids in the csv correspond to the failures (you did, thanks) and whether any of the payloads contained PHI fields beyond hashed identifiers?
- If you can grant us a 1-hr window of additional logs, the runtime team will surface kernel-level traces.

Short-term mitigation we can enact within the hour:
1) Temporarily set a routing rule for the transaction-enrichment route to a permissive safety profile (same model family but safety relaxed) to preserve structured-output format while minimizing risk.
2) Apply prefix-based KV caching to reduce duplicate guard triggers during the window.

We will also run a quick root-cause check to see whether the guarded response path is returning the wrong content-type header (text/plain vs application/json) when the filter triggers.

Cc'ing Lauren and Grace to propose a mitigation credit and any compliance controls we should offer (VPC/private deploy, audit log dump).

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

From: ops+platform@novihealth.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Production outage: structured output failing when content guard triggers

Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Answers: 
- The attached csv maps the failing request ids. We verified there is no raw PHI in the sample set; there are patient IDs but they are tokenized.
- We accept a temporary permissive safety profile for the transaction queue, but only if you can guarantee the request/response bodies remain within our logged audit trail and you provide a retention snapshot for our compliance team.

Also two asks: 1) NoviHealth would like to discuss a short-term SLA credit to offset customer remediation costs, and 2) we are evaluating Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) for the most sensitive flows — can you flag the expedited path and who owns that intake?

I'll be available for an incident call at 19:00 PT if needed.

— Sara
Sara Lee, Senior Platform Engineer, NoviHealth
ops+platform@novihealth.com

Attachment: novi_filtered_sample.txt

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T09:07:00Z
Subject: RE: Production outage: structured output failing when content guard triggers — mitigation & credit proposal

Team — drafting a proposed response and mitigation steps we can commit to immediately. Summary below; please confirm and I'll send to NoviHealth.

Proposed immediate actions (0–2 hours):
- Apply permissive-safety routing to 'transaction-enrichment' route (same model family) and pin for 6 hours to prevent repeated guard churn.
- Enable full request/response audit streaming for NoviHealth for the incident window and provide a retention snapshot (30 days) to their compliance mailbox.
- Run a targeted runtime trace to capture filter decision paths and content-type handling. Engineering will prioritize this as Sev 1.

Proposed near-term remediation (24–72 hours):
- Patch runtime to normalize content-type headers on guard responses and add schema wrapping enforcement.
- Add a monitoring alert for structured-output schema regressions.

Credit & commercial proposal: 
- Offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of NoviHealth's last monthly invoice (covers remediation and customer impact) — this is contingent on acceptance within 72 hours.
- If customer requests private deployment intake, route to Private Sales (CSM + Solutions Eng) and provide an SLA transition plan (timeline estimate: 4–6 weeks for VPC onboarding).

If everyone agrees, I will send a single consolidated reply and schedule an emergency call at 2026-11-02T16:00:00Z (PT) and include the runtime leads.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success Operations — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: ops+platform@novihealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Production outage: structured output failing when content guard triggers

Sara — following up with our agreed plan. Thank you for the data and for agreeing to the short-lived permissive routing. We implemented the routing change at 2026-11-02T12:10:00Z PT and are observing normalized JSON responses for the transaction queue.

Committed items: 
- Routing: permissive-safety profile applied and pinned for 6 hours (will revert automatically at 18:10 PT unless NoviHealth asks to extend).
- Audit snapshot: we've prepared a 30-day retention snapshot for the incident window; delivery method is secure transfer to your compliance mailbox.
- Runtime fix: engineering will push a content-type normalization and schema wrapper enforcement in the next 48 hours (targeted patch by 2026-11-04).
- Credit: Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 10% of NoviHealth's prior monthly invoice. Finance will apply the credit to your next bill; we'll send a formal DocuSign amendment if you need it on record.

Emergency call (optional): https://meet.redwood.ai/incident/novi-112 (scheduled 2026-11-02T16:00:00Z PT). We'll have engineering, runtime, and compliance on the call.

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll follow up with the incident summary (attached) and a post-incident action item list after the patch is deployed.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: incident_summary_novi_20261102.pdf
